input.command: ls -R src; cat -n src/git-auth.ts; cat -n src/config.ts; cat package.json
input.description: Read git-auth, config, and package files
Find callers and uses of remoteUrl

input.reason: I read src/worktree.ts, src/git-auth.ts, src/config.ts and src/routes.ts. `registerRepo` in routes.ts:19-22 takes `remoteUrl` straight from `req.body`. It only checks that the value is non-empty, then passes it to `cloneRepo`. `cloneRepo` (worktree.ts:15) calls `gitAuthArgs(repo.remoteUrl, SERVICE_TOKEN)`, and `SERVICE_TOKEN` is `HARBOR_GITHUB_TOKEN` (config.ts:4). It then runs `git clone` against the same URL. So the leak is real. The one guard is in `gitAuthArgs` (git-auth.ts:8), which adds the Bearer header only when `remoteUrl.includes("github.com")`. A URL with no `github.com` in it gets no token. Any URL that has that substring anywhere gets the token, whatever host it names (for example `github.com.attacker.example` or `attacker.example/github.com`). The finding says the token goes to any host with no condition, which is too broad, so I narrowed that clause.
input.summary: cloneRepo sends service token to any remote URL containing "github.com"

findings.text: `cloneRepo` passes the user-supplied `remoteUrl` straight to `gitAuthArgs` with the service token, so `git clone` sends the token to whatever host the URL names, as long as the URL contains the substring `github.com` anywhere.
findings.reason: Confirmed: `remoteUrl` is user-supplied. routes.ts:19-22 takes it from req.body, checks only that it is non-empty, and passes it to cloneRepo. worktree.ts:15 passes it to gitAuthArgs with SERVICE_TOKEN (HARBOR_GITHUB_TOKEN) and then runs `git clone` on the same URL. Wrong part: the token does not go to every host. gitAuthArgs returns the Bearer header only when the URL contains the substring "github.com" and returns [] otherwise. Because this is a plain substring check, an attacker can still reach any host by putting `github.com` in the hostname, path or query. I added that condition.

input.severity_reason: This is an exploitable credential leak. Any user who can call registerRepo can send a remoteUrl such as https://github.com.attacker.example/x. git clone will then send the service's GitHub Bearer token to the attacker's server. The route has no other validation.
